mechanism_narrative: A higher CPIAUCSL value relative to its 3-month moving average indicates persistent inflationary pressures that trigger expectations of aggressive monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds its 3-month moving average, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 4.0% signals a tight labor market that supports robust corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE is below 4.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand and economic momentum, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS exceed their 3-month moving averages, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising above 4.0% and sustained for 3 months), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced liquidity and higher discount rates.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of periods during monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.0% sustained for 3 months), or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 90.0 (2017=100 base) signals weakening economic activity and manufacturing slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO is below 90.0, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment (PAYEMS) and decrease in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market that supports consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS rises and UNRATE falls, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate above 0.5% signals an imminent monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to higher discount rates and reduced equity attractiveness.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS rises above 0.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in housing starts above 570.0 (thousands of units) signals strong consumer demand for housing, supporting economic growth and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when HOUST exceeds 570.0, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
